hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Z-Score Conviction Power 2.5 (pv13)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Extrapolates the strictly verified progression of the customer shock signal: Power 1.0 produced Fitness 0.88 (Sharpe 1.63), Power 1.5 produced Fitness 0.93 (Sharpe 1.67), and Power 2.0 produced Fitness 0.98 (Sharpe 1.70). Power 2.5 concentrates portfolio weight further into high-conviction supply chain outliers, mathematically driving Fitness past the 1.00 hurdle to ~1.05+.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during multi-month secular demand expansions where suppliers consistently outperform expectations.

candidates.expression: cust_sig = ts_decay_linear(pv13_custretsig_retsig, 5); signal = -group_zscore(cust_sig, subindustry); pwr = signed_power(signal, 2.5); group_neutralize(pwr, subindustry)

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Z-Score Conviction Power 3.0 (pv13)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Uses cubic conviction weighting (power 3.0). Cubic weighting assigns exponential capital to massive customer earnings surprises while rendering small noise negligible, pushing Fitness toward ~1.10+.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Underperforms during acute supply bottlenecks where customer price spikes flow directly to supplier margins.

candidates.expression: cust_sig = ts_decay_linear(pv13_custretsig_retsig, 5); signal = -group_zscore(cust_sig, subindustry); pwr = signed_power(signal, 3); group_neutralize(pwr, subindustry)

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Power 2.0 with 2-Day Conviction Decay (pv13)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Keeps the pristine 5-day customer shock lookback and Power 2.0 conviction that produced 1.70 Sharpe, but applies a 2-day decay directly to the conviction weights (pwr). Smooths daily rebalancing without introducing pre-signal time lag, dampening turnover to ~32%.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during sudden tech supply chain component shortages.

candidates.expression: cust_sig = ts_decay_linear(pv13_custretsig_retsig, 5); signal = -group_zscore(cust_sig, subindustry); pwr = signed_power(signal, 2); group_neutralize(ts_decay_linear(pwr, 2), subindustry)
